name: Nasr Hamid Abu Zayd
shortBio: Egyptian philosopher and Qur’anic hermeneuticist who synthesized Mu’tazilite rationalism with modern semiotics and Gadamerian hermeneutics to interpret revelation as a living dialogical text embedded in human history.
centralQuestion: How does reading the Qur’an as a historically situated linguistic and communicative discourse liberate ethical reason from literalist authoritarianism?

keyWorks.title: The Concept of the Text (Mafhum al-Nass)
keyWorks.description: Foundational Arabic hermeneutic study analyzing revelation through classical philology, Mu’tazilite theology, and modern semiotics.

keyWorks.title: Critique of Religious Discourse (Naqd al-Khitab al-Dini)
keyWorks.description: Philosophical dissection of dogmatic ideological appropriations of sacred text in contemporary Arab politics.
